$schema.purpose: Visual styles the design graph knows how to apply. A style node fixes the numbers that make a body of work look like one hand made it, so 'in the style of X' in a brief resolves to an ink colour, a stroke width and a palette rather than to each agent's own interpretation.

fields.match: phrases in a brief that name this style; the longest match wins
fields.ink: the single outline treatment used on every shape in the piece
fields.palette: named colour roles this style offers a composition; a composition chooses which it uses
fields.rules: mark-making constraints; each must be true of any shape in any piece drawn in this style

$schema.scope: A style governs MARKS — how a line and a fill are made — and nothing about what is drawn or where. Subject matter, layout and placement belong to the composition.

styles.title: Explainer cartoon — one dark ink over flat fills
rules: One ink colour for every outline in the piece — the same black on every shape, never a darker version of each fill. This single choice is most of what reads as drawn by one hand.
Flat fills only: no gradient, no shadow, no partial opacity. Depth comes from overlap and from the ink.
Parts that touch share an edge — two outlines meeting, never a gap of background between them.
One stroke weight throughout, at the width given by `ink`. Varying it per object breaks the hand.
